Aroer
ah-ROH-er
proper noun
Hebrew 'Aro'er, likely “ruins” or “bare place,” a city on the northern brink of the river Arnon, the border-marker of the Amorite kingdom.

See also: Aroer

Biblical Definition

Aroer perched on the very brink of the Arnon gorge, the frontier post of the trans-Jordan. When Israel overthrew Sihon, the conquest began here: “From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon—there was not one city too strong for us: the LORD our God delivered all unto us” (Deu 2:36). Sihon had “ruled from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the river Arnon” (Jos 12:2), and after him the town became a boundary-stone of Israel’s eastern inheritance, where David’s census-takers “pitched in Aroer” (2Sa 24:5). Centuries later, when judgment swept Moab, Aroer stood again as a lookout on the road of flight: “O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth” (Jer 48:19). A city named “ruins” watched empires rise and fall along its cliff. Aroer proclaims that no border is too strong when the LORD wills to give it, and none too secure when He wills to overthrow it. The same word that says “not one city too strong for us” also sets the watcher of Aroer to count the refugees of a fallen kingdom. Man builds his fortress on the edge of the chasm; God alone decides whether it stands as a gate of victory or a milestone of ruin.

Webster 1828 Definition

A city on the brink of the Arnon (Deu 2:36), border of the Amorite realm and later of Israel; a frontier-stone that watched empires rise and fall by the will of God.

expand to see more

AROER, a city on the northern brink of the river Arnon, east of the Dead Sea.

The starting point of Israel’s conquest of Sihon (Deu 2:36).

Sihon the Amorite had ruled from Aroer (Jos 12:2).

A border-marker of the trans-Jordan inheritance (2Sa 24:5).

A lookout on the road of Moab’s flight in judgment (Jer 48:19).

Key Scripture

Deu 2:36 — "From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the LORD our God delivered all unto us:"

Jos 12:2 — "Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and ruled from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the river Arnon,"

2Sa 24:5 — "And they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that lieth in the midst of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:"

Jer 48:19 — "O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth, and say, What is done?"

Modern Corruption

A frontier city on the Arnon; the entry recovers that no border is too strong to be given, nor too secure to be overthrown, when the LORD wills.

expand to see more

Aroer raises no modern controversy, but its cliff-top vigil rebukes the confidence of the fortified. Men set their strongest cities on the edge of the chasm and call them impregnable; yet at Aroer there was not one city too strong for the LORD to give, and the same Aroer became a watch-post over Moab’s ruin.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the LORD’s absolute sway over the rise and fall of powers. The nations trust their frontiers and their arms, but the God of Israel delivers the strong city into the hands He chooses and sends the watcher to count the refugees of the proud. Aroer preaches that history is not the story of the strong prevailing, but of the Almighty ruling; and the wise man builds his hope not on the cliff’s edge but on the Rock.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Aro'er, “ruins” or “bare place,” a border city on the brink of the Arnon.

Aroer — Hebrew 'Aro'er, likely “ruins” or “bare place.”

A city on the northern brink of the river Arnon.

The frontier from which Sihon ruled and Israel’s conquest began.

A border-marker of the trans-Jordan inheritance.

A lookout over the flight of Moab in the day of judgment (Jer 48:19).

Usage

"Israel’s conquest began from Aroer on the brink of Arnon."

"David’s census-men pitched in Aroer by the river of Gad."

"Aroer preaches that no fortress is too strong when the LORD wills to give it."
